newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-Injuries hit NZ bowlers yet again.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-Injuries hit NZ bowlers yet again.

text.p: Sharjah, Nov 14 - New Zealand have been forced to radically rethink their strategy for the Champions Trophy one-day cricket series final against Pakistan here tonight.

A sequence of appalling collapses at the top of the order will see either Mark Greatbatch or captain Lee Germon open alongside Bryan Young, with Craig Spearman being omitted after a series of low scores.

Stephen Fleming, dropped two days ago after scratching out just 15 runs in three innings, has been recalled to the team in spectacular fashion, while the New Zealanders enter the tri-nations tournament final without their strike bowlers Danny
"But, if the requirements of the team are that I open, then I'll do it.
"Mark Greatbatch feels much the same way. He's a guy who thrives on responsibility and he can be inspirational."

Greatbatch has played in the middle order during this tournament and has tempered his natural inclination to hit high and hard. Instead, he has looked to paddle the ball away into the gaps for ones and two, collecting at a much more sedate pace than the Greatbatch who enlivened the 1992 World Cup as an opener.
Germon, who scored 52 in the last preliminary game against Pakistan on Wednesday when batting at No 8, had previously voiced his reluctance to be shunted up the order to No 3.
However, he now believes the team's needs must come first, and he is prepared to confront the feared Pakistan fast bowling attack head-on if need be.
"It would only be a one off and it's not a long term proposition," Germon said.
"In the interests of my own game I think I find it very difficult to bat for a long time then keep wickets and lead the side.
"Whichever way we go, with either Paddy or myself, we will approach it positively," Germon said.
"We won't be going in to act as pinch hitters, we'll be positive and we'll be up front."
Adam Parore, with two half-centuries in Sharjah, and Nathan Astle were other contenders to share the opening duties with Young.
But Germon said both of these players had other roles to play.
"Adam is very comfortable at number three. He was considered but I think he is confident at three whereas I think Nathan can be of more benefit to us in the middle order against these guys."
The loss of Doull and Morrison are hard crucial blows to New Zealand.

Their absence deprives the attack of penetration and pace, a combination which has served New Zealand well here as they made inroads into the opposition in the formative stages of the innings in three of the four preliminary matches.
Pakistan captain and left arm fast bowler Wasim Akram missed the last preliminary match because of a shoulder complaint, but the New Zealanders fully expect him to play tonight.
NEW ZEALAND: Lee Germon (captain), Bryan Young, Mark Greatbatch, Adam Parore, Stephen Fleming, Nathan Astle, Chris Cairns, Chris Harris, Justin Vaughan, Dipak Patel, Gavin Larsen.

PAKISTAN (from): Wasim Akram (captain). Saeed Anwar, Aamir Sohail, Ijaz Ahmed, Salim Malik, Hasan Raza, Saqlain Mushtaq, Shahid Afridi, Moin Khan, Waqar Younis, Shahid Nazir, Abdul Raazaq, Azam Kahn, Mustaq Ahmed.
